# ASVS 5.0.0 L2: V7 Session Management

> Self-assessment against OWASP ASVS 5.0.0, Level 2, chapter V7 Session Management: not yet assessed by a person. The entries below are the working state, filled in with tests and code pointers; the maintainer's first pass and second pass are still to come. This is not a certification, and no independent party has reviewed it. OWASP does not certify projects.

Status: **in progress**. 17 pass, 0 n/a, 1 fail.

Existing sessions kept the ends they were created with; the document says so. |
| **7.1.2** Verify that the documentation defines how many concurrent (parallel) sessions are allowed for one account as well as the intended behaviors and actions to be taken when the maximum number of active sessions is reached. | L2 | pass | doc [docs/security/sessions.md](../../../docs/security/sessions.md) | docs/security/sessions.md defines the number of concurrent sessions as unlimited, the behaviour at a limit as none (no session is ever ended to make room), and why; the control is the session list and its termination (7.5.2). | **7.4.1** Verify that when session termination is triggered (such as logout or expiration), the application disallows any further use of the session. For reference tokens or stateful sessions, this means invalidating the session data at the application backend. Applications using self-contained tokens will need a solution such as maintaining a list of terminated tokens, disallowing tokens produced before a per-user date and time or rotating a per-user signing key. | L1 | pass | test `[ASVS-7.4.1]`<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/sessions.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/sessions.ts) | Logout, log out everywhere and expiry delete or stop the row; other server processes may accept a revoked session for at most the 5 s cache TTL (ADR-0007). |
| **7.4.2** Verify that the application terminates all active sessions when a user account is disabled or deleted (such as an employee leaving the company). | L1 | pass | test `[ASVS-7.4.2]`<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/sessions.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/sessions.ts)<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/approval.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/approval.ts)<br>doc [docs/security/sessions.md](../../../docs/security/sessions.md) | sessions.resolve refuses a session whose user is not active or is deleted, on every uncached lookup. Rejecting a user revokes all their sessions in the same transaction, and every path that ends sessions (logout, log out everywhere, ending one from the list, the administrators' termination, rejecting an account) empties this process's cache entries at once; the cache is not left to run out. Across server processes a session may still be accepted for at most the 5 s cache TTL (docs/security/sessions.md, ADR-0007); there is no cross-process invalidation. No disable-account feature exists yet (backlog); when it does it must call revokeAll and get its own test. |
